edit.description: `binding_limit()` (:230) has been the binding-limit sentence's one home since b817cb25, rendering `GUARD_MATCHER` (:149)'s own alternation for prose, but it is private — so the external `it` crate cannot read it and its surface pin spells the sentence by hand instead. Make it `pub`, with its doc naming the consumer the export is opened for (the block-mode guard surface pin), the shape this module already models: `SESSION_START_COMMAND` (:105) and `GUARD_COMMAND` (:168) are `pub` precisely so the gate-wiring asserts read the writer's own bytes rather than a copy. Rider on the same file, discharging prose the fold left behind: `guard`'s doc (:1204) still hand-holds the limit in a `**Binding scope**` paragraph that re-spells the tool list ("Write, Edit, MultiEdit tools") a third time beside `GUARD_MATCHER`'s literal and its own doc — it points at `binding_limit()` instead, per engineering.md's narration ladder, now that a pin and an export hold the property.

`guard_reads_the_block_mode_from_the_lock_not_the_retired_manifest` (:1525) asserts the guard's stderr `contains` the whole composed sentence, tool list included, as a literal (:1548) — a stored copy of a value derived from `GUARD_MATCHER`, so widening the matcher turns this test red for the wrong reason and the fix on offer is to re-copy. It reads `install::binding_limit()` instead (the module is already imported as `install::{self, ..}` at :31), keeping the claim the assertion was widened to make — the tail reaches the user in full — while the expected bytes come from the writer. The file's two other matcher literals stay and the entry must not touch them: `assert_gate_hooks_wired` (:622) and the scaffolded guard module's `matcher:` field (:1260) pin the wire value Claude Code reads, which with the fresh-install settings snapshot is where the cited provider fact is reviewed — a value pin, not a derived copy.

summary: The guard's surface pin stores a hand copy of the binding-limit sentence, tool list included, so widening GUARD_MATCHER turns the CLI test red for the wrong reason.

tests.asserts: the block-mode guard's stderr carries `install::binding_limit()` verbatim, with no hand-spelled copy of the sentence or its tool list left in the file

acceptance: `cargo test` green with `rg -n 'This guard binds only' tests/` returning nothing — the sentence has one home in `src/install.rs` and the surface pin reads it — plus `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all --check`.
notes: Residue of b817cb25's own remedy: nothing asserted the tail reached the user before, so that entry added the surface pin and spelled the sentence by hand. The export is not a reinstatement of the `GUARD_MESSAGE` one the same commit retired for want of a reader — this one names its consumer, the shape `GUARD_COMMAND` already has here. scoped at b4608cc7
